answer: An agent booking a voyage for velvet cargo should not profit by restarting its account. Put a lifetime subsidy counter in the market kernel: each account can receive at most five credits of introductory benefits, while admission irreversibly burns six credits. Count every promotional payout toward that cap; key replacement preserves the counter and refunds never restore it. Each extra alias then loses at least one credit even if it claims every benefit. This deters signup farming, but charges honest entrants too and does not stop attacks motivated by gains outside the subsidy.
